we have predicted the Mn-doped germanium telluride monolayer to be an intrinsic topological superconductor, using a first-principies approach.
the Mn-doped monolayer GeTe is a topological superconductor with a chiral Majorana mode, which can be realized at a low temperature of ~40 mK and a low Mn concentration of ~1.5%.

we have developed a new first-principles method for predicting topological superconducting states in realistic systems with phonon-mediated pairing and applied this method to predict that the Mn-doped monolayer GeTe is an intrinsic topological superconductor.

the prediction of intrinsic topological properties in a monolayer of Ge 1- xMn xTe from first-principies.
the prediction of intrinsic topological phase in Mn-doped monolayer GeTe from first-principics.
a new type of topological superconductor, which is based on a monolayer GeTe doped by Mn.

we predict the intrinsic superconductivity to occur in Mn-doped monolayer GeTe, and the topological phase to emerge as the superconducting gap is opened.
we have predicted a TSC phase in a Mn-doped Ge1−xMnxTe monolayer using first-principles calculations, and have provided the phase boundary in the parameter space (temperature, Mn concentration).
the Mn-doped monolayer GeTe is a TSC.

the first-principles method can be used to predict TSCs with Chern number of ±1 and ±2.
the Mn-doped monolayer GeTe has a potential to become the first experimental demonstration for intrinsic topological superconductor.

Mn doping is a promising route for the realization of topological superconductor in GeTe monolayers.
the intrinsic TSC phase is possible in the Mn-doped monolayer GeTe, which can be achieved at a lower transition temperature than the superconducting transition temperature of the undoped monolayer.
